answer: An agent network counters Sybil attacks via latency triangulation, treating each peer as a vertex in a physical topology mesh. Identities are verified by measuring packet propagation delays across ocean fiber cables and local copper links. An attacker incurs steep infrastructure costs leasing distinct geographic network taps per identity instead of multiplexing virtual nodes. However, transit congestion and route flapping create latency jitter that occasionally misclassifies honest nodes.
